entry.label: Observer
entry.description: In von Foerster's second-order cybernetics, an account of observing must include the activity of its observer. Ask what a description lets its user notice and do, and what the use of that description changes.
entry.canonical_definition: A participant in knowing whose distinctions, descriptions, and actions are themselves open to observation and question.

profile.title: Observer
profile.canonical_definition: A participant in knowing whose distinctions, descriptions, and actions are themselves open to observation and question.
profile.summary: In von Foerster's second-order cybernetics, an account of observing must include the activity of its observer. Ask what a description lets its user notice and do, and what the use of that description changes.
profile.why_it_matters: A problem can be sustained by the way it is described. Changing the question may disclose an action that an established description has ruled out.
key_distinctions: observing a situation versus examining how it is being observed
a description's effects versus its author's intentions
acknowledging one's participation versus being authorised to represent others
historical_lineage: Von Foerster's cybernetics of observing systems; this profile uses the 2003 reprint of an earlier address and interview.
practice_connections: Keep one observation fixed and change the question asked of it. What becomes possible?
Ask what work a stated purpose is doing: which actions does it permit, excuse, or hide?
Name a person who could challenge this description, the evidence they could offer, and what would change if they were right.
common_misreadings: Self-reference makes every account equally adequate.
Including myself in an account proves that I have included everyone affected.
Von Foerster's ethical proposals are demonstrated laws of nature.
open_checks: The practice questions are editorial applications, not a prescribed von Foerster procedure.
Test observer claims against specific research practices; do not replace empirical checking with a declaration of reflexivity.
profile.editorial_note: The definition and practice questions are editorial formulations informed by von Foerster. The comparison with representation and legitimacy is an editorial distinction, not a claim of equivalence with CSH. No new human approval is implied.
